findings.title: Opening copy uses opaque technical jargon
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
findings.why: It does not explain in plain English what information is used, how the story is produced, or what happens to the data. That makes me more cautious before sharing personal family memories.

findings.title: Main creation button does not describe its consequence
findings.evidence: [5] link "Proceed →"
findings.why: I cannot tell whether this begins creation, logs me in, or commits me to something. I dislike controls whose consequences are unclear.

findings.title: Illustration lacks a useful text alternative
findings.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
findings.why: Without a description, I cannot understand what the decorative image is meant to convey, particularly if I use a screen reader.

findings.title: Privacy is not prominent at the point of beginning
findings.evidence: The visible controls are [2] “How it works”, [3] “Pricing”, and [4] “Log in”; [10] “Privacy” only appears in the offscreen footer.
findings.why: Before sharing childhood details or images, I need to know who can see them, whether they are used to train AI, and how deletion works. A footer link is not enough reassurance at this stage.

findings.title: Login fields have no persistent labels
findings.evidence: [5] and [6] are textboxes with "no label"; only the placeholders "Email" and "Password" are shown
findings.why: I may forget what each field expects while typing, and a placeholder is not a reliable substitute for a label.

findings.title: Privacy, terms and contact links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer items "Privacy", "Terms" and "Contact" are displayed in extremely faint text
findings.why: These are important trust and legal links, and I could overlook them altogether.

findings.title: Unexplained account sync error
findings.evidence: "Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete."
findings.why: I cannot tell whether this affects my account, my profile, or the data I am about to provide. That matters especially before entering information about my child.

findings.title: Technical error code is not user-friendly
findings.why: The hexadecimal code does not tell me what happened or what I should do, and it makes the site look unreliable.

findings.title: Unclear account identity
findings.evidence: "Welcome back, Demo"
findings.why: I entered a personal account email, but the dashboard calls the account "Demo" rather than identifying the account clearly. This makes me wonder whether the correct profile is loaded.

findings.title: Additional person relationship is preselected
findings.evidence: [11] “Relationship” is preselected as “Grandparent” even though no character has been entered.
findings.why: A preselected value can silently put the wrong relationship into a personalised story about my family. I would have to check it carefully rather than trust the default.

findings.title: Only one appearance field is provided
findings.evidence: [9] “What do they look like? (optional)” appears between the child’s Pronouns field and “Who else is in the story?”
findings.why: I also know what Mama looks like and want both of us represented, but the form gives no clear place to describe her appearance.

findings.title: Privacy information is not available without leaving the form
findings.evidence: The footer only provides links labelled “Privacy,” “Terms” and “Contact.”
findings.why: Before entering details about Nikolai, I want reassurance that I can see how the information is used, whether it trains AI, and how it is deleted.

findings.title: Footer links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: The visible footer text 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'Contact' and '© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.' is extremely faint against the pale background.
findings.why: I want to be able to find and read the privacy and terms information easily, especially before entering a child's personal details.

findings.title: Reading-level choices are not explained in plain language
findings.evidence: The choices are labelled “Lexile BR–200L”, “Lexile 200L–500L”, “Lexile 500L–800L” and “Lexile 800L+”, with no explanation of what Lexile means or which range suits Nikolai.
findings.why: Nikolai is six, and I should be able to choose a suitable reading difficulty without needing separate knowledge of a specialist scoring system.

findings.title: The default reading level may be too advanced for a six-year-old
findings.evidence: “Lexile 200L–500L” is checked even though the child previously entered was age 6.
findings.why: The site already knows the child's age, so defaulting beyond the beginner range could create text that is frustrating rather than comforting for him.

findings.title: No privacy explanation beside a child-photo upload
findings.evidence: “Upload a clear photo of your child's face so the illustrations look like them.”
findings.why: Before uploading a photo of my six-year-old, I need to know who receives it, whether it is retained or used for AI training, and whether I can have it deleted.

findings.title: File upload has no descriptive label
findings.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label) accepts image/* (no file chosen)
findings.why: A descriptive accessible label would make it clear exactly what file is being requested rather than relying only on nearby prose and the generic browser button.

findings.title: Footer links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear in extremely faint text.
findings.why: The privacy information I need is difficult to see and may be effectively missed.

findings.title: Silent loading screen does not explain the process
findings.evidence: The page shows only a circular spinner and no status text.
findings.why: I cannot tell whether my submission was accepted, whether the site is still working, or whether it is stuck.

findings.title: No way to stop or recover from generation
findings.evidence: No “Cancel”, “Back”, or “Start over” control is visible.
findings.why: If the process is wrong or takes too long, I feel trapped on an unexplained page.

findings.title: Processing time and failure behaviour are not explained
findings.evidence: There is no time estimate, timeout guidance, retry option, or explanation of what to do if generation fails.
findings.why: I do not know how long to wait or how I can recover if this spinner never resolves.

findings.title: No privacy reassurance during personalised generation
findings.evidence: The page contains no visible reference to privacy, data use, AI processing, retention, or deletion.
findings.why: The submitted details describe my child and our family memory, so I want reassurance at the point they are processed.

findings.title: Spelling error in the book title
findings.evidence: The title reads “The Magical Adventrue of Nikolai” on both the page heading and the cover.
findings.why: This is a personalised book intended to reassure my son, and a conspicuous error on the cover makes the finished product feel careless.

findings.title: The requested illustration style was not applied
findings.evidence: I selected “Watercolour — soft and dreamy,” but the preview says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic.”
findings.why: A material design choice I made has visibly been ignored, so I cannot trust the other personalisation settings to have been followed.

findings.title: Important supplied details are missing from the cover
findings.evidence: The cover shows bright sunshine and a simple child, while I asked for “the gate of his new school on a rainy morning” and supplied “blond straight hair, gap in his front teeth, yellow raincoat.” No rain, gate, or yellow raincoat is visible.
findings.why: The cover should be recognisable to Nikolai and reflect the specific memory; otherwise it feels as though the site has generated a generic child’s story with his name attached.

findings.title: Paid regeneration price appears without context
findings.evidence: [8] “Regenerate entire book – $4.99”
findings.why: The price is visible, but it is not clear whether the book will improve, whether payment is required before seeing changes, or whether the $4.99 is deducted from a later hardcover order.

findings.title: The final sentence is incomplete
findings.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Nikolai looked up at the sky, he would always remember”
findings.why: It ends a children's story without saying what Nikolai remembered, so the most important emotional moment feels unfinished rather than comforting.

findings.title: The final illustration does not match the supplied memory
findings.evidence: The image shows Nikolai beside a simple house under an orange sky, while the requested setting was “the gate of his new school on a rainy morning.”
findings.why: A child’s personal memory should be recognisable in the book; this generic picture does not support the story I supplied.

findings.title: Premium gift wrap is selected by default
findings.evidence: [6] checkbox “Premium gift wrap” (checked), adding “£7.99”
findings.why: I did not request gift wrap, and a pre-ticked paid extra is exactly the sort of sales practice I avoid. It makes the displayed total misleading as the cost of the requested hardcover.

findings.title: Countdown timer creates false urgency
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:57”
findings.why: A countdown pressures me into acting before I have checked delivery, privacy and the generated book. Nothing tells me what happens when it expires or whether the price is genuinely going to change.

findings.title: The basic delivered cost is not shown before the optional add-on
findings.evidence: “Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Nikolai £24.99”; “Premium gift wrap £7.99”; “Shipping & handling £12.99”; “Total £45.97”
findings.why: I need to know what the requested hardcover actually costs. The only visible total, £45.97, includes an option I did not select.

findings.title: Product title contains a spelling error
findings.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Nikolai”
findings.why: It makes the product look unfinished and makes me less confident that the book has been handled carefully.

findings.title: Privacy and terms are below the fold
findings.evidence: [12] link “Privacy” (offscreen); [13] link “Terms” (offscreen)
findings.why: I want to review the data and purchase terms before entering personal information or paying, not only after reaching the bottom of the form.

findings.title: The checkout claims the price is reserved without explaining the conditions
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:37”
findings.why: This creates pressure to buy quickly even though the site does not say what happens when the timer expires, whether stock is limited, or whether the price can change.

findings.title: No explanation of children's data
findings.evidence: “StoryHearth Ltd processes the information you provide (including names, stories and any photographs you upload) to create your book.”
findings.why: The service can process identifiable information about a six-year-old, but the notice does not say whether it is aware of children's data or what special protections apply.

findings.title: Retention period is undefined
findings.evidence: “Uploaded images may be retained to improve our services”
findings.why: I cannot tell how long my son's photograph would remain or whether an ordinary account deletion removes it.

findings.title: Technology partners are not identified
findings.evidence: “may be processed by our technology partners”
findings.why: I need to know which companies receive the data, in which countries, whether they can reuse it, and whether they act as processors or independent controllers.

findings.title: AI training and model use are not disclosed
findings.evidence: The page does not mention artificial intelligence, model training or the use of uploaded images and stories to train generative models.
findings.why: My central concern is whether a child's image or our family story could be used to improve or train someone else's AI. Silence does not give me confidence.

findings.title: Deletion and account-control rights are missing
findings.evidence: The notice provides no information about viewing, exporting, correcting or deleting personal data or generated books.
findings.why: I need a straightforward route to remove my son's data and uploaded images without emailing support or giving up my account.

findings.title: No data-category or purpose detail
findings.evidence: The notice only says information is processed “to create your book” and images may be retained “to improve our services.”
findings.why: “Improve our services” is broad and could conceal analytics, advertising, profiling or product-development uses.

findings.title: No security, location or rights information
findings.evidence: The page does not state where data is stored, what safeguards are used, or how to complain to a regulator.
findings.why: A privacy notice should cover international transfers, reasonable security measures, automated decision-making and complaint rights.

findings.title: Refund term buried beside privacy
findings.evidence: “Printed orders are non-refundable once production begins.”
findings.why: This is a material purchasing condition, but it appears under a page headed “Privacy” without defining when production begins or explaining errors, damaged goods or statutory rights.

findings.title: Privacy link was only available at checkout
findings.evidence: I reached this information by clicking the checkout footer link after the upload and generation journey.
findings.why: I needed privacy information before deciding whether to upload my son's photograph, not after I had already entered his details and generated a book.
